title: daemon stop and restart cope with a daemon that predates daemon.stop
lead: Seen 2026-10-20: after S46 landed, the owner ran ork daemon restart against the daemon started before it. The new CLI warned 'stale daemon build unknown differs from CLI build ...' (daemon.info reported unknown, as designed), then failed with 'ork: unknown method daemon.stop'. The old daemon cannot be told to stop, so the owner had to kill it by pid again. Every upgrade past a daemon that lacks daemon.stop hits this once.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The command meant to remove the need to kill the daemon by pid fails on exactly the daemon that needs replacing. The error does not say what to do.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- internal/cli/lifecycle.go: daemonCommand stop call and its error at :89-93. The restart path (:116-122) is not reached when the stop fails this way. daemonBuild (:22-24) already checks for CodeUnknownMethod; use the same check.
- internal/cli/cli.go:72-82: App gets a Pid field beside Socket (:77). Run (:88-93) sets it.
- cmd/ork/main.go:115 and :144: the two other App constructions set Pid from paths.Pid.
- internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go: new test beside TestOldDaemonUnknownBuildMethod (:52). TestDaemonStopClosesSocket (:168) and TestDaemonRestartServesAgain (:186) must keep passing.
- docs/design.md:39-58 (stop and restart, including the unknown_method note near :58) and :545-546 (commands).
- internal/daemon: no change. The pid file is already written (daemon.go:162-166) and its path is in daemon.Paths (daemon.go:36-44). Decision 118: ork does not signal the pid.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `ork daemon stop` against a daemon that answers unknown_method to daemon.stop says the daemon predates the stop command, gives the pid from the pid file, and shows `kill -TERM PID`. The output does not contain "unknown method".
- `ork daemon restart` against the same daemon prints the same guidance and starts no daemon.
- The guidance warns when a role is running (the source is Open in Implement).
- ork sends no signal: the child process named as the pid is still alive after the command.
- After the old daemon exits, `ork daemon restart` starts the new daemon (pattern: TestDaemonRestartServesAgain, internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go:186).
- A daemon that answers daemon.stop still stops as before (TestDaemonStopClosesSocket, internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go:168).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing test first in internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go, beside TestOldDaemonUnknownBuildMethod (:52). Use its fake server, but answer daemon.stop with unknown_method. Set App.Pid to the pid of a live child process the test starts. Assert the output says the daemon predates the stop command, names the pid and shows `kill -TERM PID`, does not contain "unknown method", and that the child is still alive afterwards.
2. Add `Pid string` to App (internal/cli/cli.go:72-82) beside Socket (:77). It holds the daemon's pid file and is used only for the stop hint.
3. Set it where App is built: internal/cli/cli.go:93 (Run), cmd/ork/main.go:115 and :144 (paths.Pid is in scope there).
4. In daemonCommand, after the stop call fails (internal/cli/lifecycle.go:89-93), check for an ipc.Error with Code daemon.CodeUnknownMethod, as daemonBuild does (lifecycle.go:22-23). If it matches, read a.Pid, print the message to stderr, and return a failure code (the code is Open).
5. Message (*proposed* wording): "daemon predates daemon.stop; pid PID; stop it with: kill -TERM PID". If a.Pid cannot be read, print the pid file path and say so.
6. Warn when a role is running, as decision 118 says. The source is Open.
7. Other errors keep the existing o.failErr path (lifecycle.go:92-93).
8. ork does not signal the pid. Restart uses the same branch, so lifecycle.go:116-122 is not reached. The owner runs the printed kill, then ork daemon restart.
9. Update docs/design.md:39-58 and :545-546.
Open: (a) the exit code for stop and restart in this case; decision 118 does not say. (b) Where "a role is running" comes from when the old daemon may not answer status: the field is RolesRunning (internal/daemon/handlers.go:191), and an old daemon may not know it. (c) The wording is *proposed*.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli/...`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` (prints nothing)
- `slicer check`
- `rg -n "unknown method" internal/cli --glob '!*_test.go'`: the stop path must not print the raw error any more.
- TestStaleDaemonCommandWarning (internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go:291) and TestDaemonStopClosesSocket (:168) still pass.
- No test signals a pid other than the child process the test starts.
